intro: Professionals and everyday users convert pints (us) (pt) to liters (L) when working across us_customary and metric standards in culinary recipe scaling, beverage bottling, laboratory reagent preparation, and fluid tank capacity sizing. One pint (us liquid) equals 0.473176 liters, while 1 liter equals 2.113376 pints (us). Whether you are verifying volume & liquid specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: US Customary vs. British Imperial Liquid Volume Trap
items: US Customary and UK Imperial liquid units share identical names but have different physical volumes: 1 US Gallon is 3.78541 L (128 US fl oz), whereas 1 UK Imperial Gallon is 4.54609 L (160 Imp fl oz) — a 20.1% difference.

Similarly, 1 US Pint contains 16 US fluid ounces (473.18 mL), while 1 British Imperial Pint contains 20 Imperial fluid ounces (568.26 mL). Always verify whether your recipe, pump datasheet, or vehicle spec sheet uses US or UK standards.

faqs.question: How many liters (L) are in 1 pint (us liquid) (pt)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.47317647 liters (L) in 1 pint (us liquid) (pt), which rounds to 0.4732 L for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 liter equals 2.113376 pints (us).

faqs.question: How do I convert pints (us) to liters (pt to L)?
faqs.answer: To convert pints (us) to liters, use the formula: L = pt × 0.47317647. For example, converting 10 pt gives 4.7318 L.

faqs.question: What is 10 pints (us) in liters?
faqs.answer: 10 pints (us) (pt) equals exactly 4.7318 liters (L) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
